summary: The only held-name print in the window is WMT on 11-19, which the company has confirmed, 2 trading days out. The open question about WMT's 11-16 8-K 5.02 now looks answered: the same-day headline says Caterpillar CEO Joe Creed joined the board, effective immediately. That reads as a director appointment, not an executive departure, though this is an inference from item numbers plus the headline. ADSK, BBY and BLBD are now inside the 5-day window for a new buy. CART has a new DOJ antitrust review of the DoorDash deal. Today's feed is different from earlier runs: it has only single-company fiscal.ai items and nothing tagged BTC, ETH, QQQ, VOO, VTI or the bond and gold ETFs, and no Nvidia headline. So I can't update the crypto, rates or Nvidia threads today. That is a gap in the input, not a calm tape.

A director election is a 5.02 event, so the filing most likely records an appointment, not an executive departure. This is an inference: the filing text is not in my input, but no headline suggests anyone left. BNP's $144 PT (11-16) is the latest of about eleven raises in seven sessions, so the bar for the print is high. As L7 notes, a stop based on the close does not protect against a gap on the print. Today's other WMT items (China provincial agreement, holiday product launches, Operation Homefront) are noise.

notable.headline: Walmart Appoints Caterpillar CEO Joe Creed to Board of Directors (11-16)
notable.read: This most likely explains the 8-K 5.02/9.01 filed the same day, which I left open on 11-16 as possibly an executive departure three days before the print. A new director is the benign reading of a 5.02. Treat it as resolved by inference, not by reading the filing. That leaves the 11-19 print itself, against crowded bullish PT drift, as WMT's only live event.

notable.headline: US Justice Department to Review DoorDash's Acquisition of Instacart
notable.read: The 10-27 deal flag came true as the $65 DoorDash agreement on 10-29. Now the deal faces an antitrust review, which adds time and break risk to the deal spread. Anyone proposing CART is underwriting the regulator, not the business.
